title: Cyril Against Julian Book 4
english: People often oppose those who grieve and resist their enemies with equal anger, but when it comes to children, they spare them; however, they take pleasure in human blood and gaze upon the altars of the gods with delight, considering it a delight to sacrifice human beings.
According to Julian, they have this tendency naturally, as he says.
Someone might say that we are merely playing with words by intending to imply a criminology in those things, for it is not as if such things had ever happened to men.
Let us examine, therefore, from the Greek historians, whether they did not indeed pollute their altars and temples with human blood and sacrifices.

Aristomenes the Messenian was grateful to Jupiter for the three hundred dead bodies, and he was also grateful to the Lacedaemonian kings, and this one added the king, and from there the highest and greatest of the gods, and the prince of the gods, who pitied the wretched and saw their full altar.

It was a custom for men to make their own misfortunes a delight, and the Scythians, who lived around the Tauric Chersonese, would intercept and kill strangers and hang their heads on the temple doors as an offering to the goddess, and they would bring her human slaughter as a gift.
To them, it would seem more cruel to snatch away the hope of salvation from those who had escaped, merely showing the pretext of death.

Erechtheus of the Athenians, having been approached by subterranean daemons, is said to have cruelly slaughtered his own daughter, as Dorotheus, a historian, reports in the fourth book of his histories.
Monymus also reports, in the collection of wonders, the immolation of Peleus and Chiron in the city of Pellene in Thrace, and that the altar of Dionysus in Lesbos was imbued with the blood of men.
While the pagan superstition was still strong, gladiatorial contests were held at Rome, and some were hidden under the earth with perforated stones, so that the blood of the fallen would pollute.

Porphyry writes in his second book about abstaining from animate things, thus: 'History is about not only what Theophrastus remembered, but also many other things, that humans were sacrificed.', and this is fully recorded in history.
For in Rhodes, in the month of Meta, on the sixth day, a human was sacrificed to Agraulos, the daughter of Cecrops and the nymph Agraulis, in the city of Salamis, which was previously called Coronis.
This custom continued until the time of Diomedes, when it was changed, and a temple of Minerva was built, and the sacrifice of humans to Agraulos and Diomedes was stopped.

Furthermore, the one to be immolated, who was from Athens and Agra, and who was led by ephebes, went around the altar three times; then the priest struck him with a knife in the stomach, and the pyre was set on fire, burning him completely.

They also sacrificed humans in Chios and Tenedos, and the Phoenicians sacrificed humans to Saturn, saying that the slaughter of humans was a sacrifice to the gods, but it was not to the gods, rather to the evil demons.

The Cretans, on the other hand, sacrificed the Curetes to Cronus, and the altars of the gods were polluted with the blood of miserable humans, which the Greeks believed was a delight for them, but not for the gods, rather for the evil demons.

They would place Saturn and Jupiter and Mars and the sister of Castor, and they would rejoice in the stupid Bacchus and the sister of Apollo, and they would worship them, showing that they were actually worshiping evil demons, not the gods.

title: On Sacrificial Practice and Divine Worship
english: …They hold a place among the gods, to whom the bloody sacrifice of Semele was offered, or among the Greeks who are conspicuous for their sacrifices; and who are they that help? Either they are abominable demons, to be shunned by the gods, and impious and wicked, or, if they say that sacrifices are offered to them, they are either gods or demons, and they accuse them of being cruel and wicked, or they concede that they are demons of wickedness, or they are written about by us as being the same as the gods, or they are the ones who have reached the utmost limit of cruelty and are hated and execrated, and they ask what kind of demon would be the one to whom sacrifices are offered, and they are already refuted by their own actions, and they are impure and abominable demons, and all are said to be guilty of extreme wickedness, and if anyone were to become such, what misery!

For what is worse than being polluted and infamous, and having reached the lowest causes, that they have become murderers of men, and all have been made to suffer? If someone were to become such a thing, what misery! The Scythian woman, a murderer and magician, is a prime example of this. She was once a loving wife, but later, overcome by her own desires, she willed the death of her children, and became a tragic figure, a story and a tragic plot. This story is a testament to the miserable death of the father, and the wild and savage nature of the Scythian woman, who cultivated evil spirits and was a magician. These are the ones who have been given over to the demons, and have been permitted by the creator of all things to indulge in licentiousness. Since, as they say, they have already been proven by their own actions, they are the ones who are wicked and abominable, and not others.

They were offering sacrifices to detestable demons and all kinds of foulness, not to gods, but to demons; and they were building temples in all regions and cities, and they were sacrificing to these demons, saying that these demons were standing over them. They were asking how they could be pleasing to these demons, and they were building altars to them, and they were making sacrifices to them, and they were saying that they were honoring them, but they were not honoring them, but rather the demons, for they were standing over them, by the grace of the Creator of all things. For it is written: 'The angel of the Lord will encamp around those who fear him and rescue them' (Psalm 33:8).

To live a great and noble life, we must first recognize that if we make the will of a good and blameless life great, and with a pure and unblemished zeal for goodness, we shall strive to be assimilated to the all-holy God. We shall attempt to succeed in this by using sacrifices that are pleasing to Him, and we must be cautious of the evil spirits that seek to lead us astray. The soul must be purified in every way, and this can be achieved by fleeing from impious demons and seeking refuge in the divine. As Hermes Trismegistus wrote, one must strive to be pious, chaste, and innocent, for it is only then that God will rescue us from all evil.
Since they are already proven by their own actions, they are the ones who are wicked and abominable, and not others. Because of this, they are being led into such things.
…Since they are being led into such things...
